prerequisites: Fundamental knowledge of Applied Mechanics of Machines provided in the basic 6 CFU module.
Basic knowledge of Physics, Mathematical Analysis, Geometry, and Technical Drawing.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the fundamental principles of human biomechanics and the basic methodologies for analyzing stresses acting on body segments during daily activities.
Apply mechanical and biomechanical principles to analyze loading conditions and stresses in the main segments of the human body.
Critically evaluate the results of biomechanical analyses, interpreting the effects of loading conditions on the behavior of body segments.
Describe the adopted methodologies and obtained results in biomechanical analyses using appropriate technical terminology.
Independently develop the ability to explore methodologies and tools for human biomechanical analysis through technical texts and scientific documentation.
Understand the fundamental principles of rigid body mechanics and mechanical systems, with particular reference to mechanical drives and power transmission systems.
Apply mechanical methodologies to address problems related to mechanical systems and develop numerical models using computational tools, such as electronic spreadsheets.
Evaluate modeling assumptions and select appropriate methodologies for solving mechanical problems, critically interpreting the results obtained from numerical analyses.
Describe the adopted procedures, the developed models, and the obtained results using appropriate technical terminology and clear engineering documentation.
Independently use software tools and computational methodologies for the analysis of mechanical systems and for further exploration of engineering applications.

syllabus_topics: In-depth study of specific topics in Applied Mechanics of Machines and their practical applications
Development of methodologies for the analysis and solution of mechanical system problems
Learning the use of Microsoft Excel or other electronic spreadsheet tools for the implementation and numerical solution of mechanical system models
Processing and graphical representation of the trends of the main kinematic and dynamic variables obtained from numerical simulations
Biomechanical properties of biological tissues
Bone tissue: structural characteristics and mechanical behavior
Articular cartilage: functional properties and role in joint biomechanics
Tendons and ligaments: mechanical characteristics and function within the musculoskeletal system
Muscles: biomechanical properties and role in motion generation
Biomechanical analysis of human movement
Principles of human body mobility
Analysis of human motion and interactions between body segments
Biomechanics of major joints
Biomechanical analysis of the knee
Biomechanical analysis of the hip
Biomechanical analysis of the ankle
Biomechanical analysis of the lumbar spine
Biomechanical analysis of the shoulder
Biomechanical analysis of the elbow
Engineering approach to posture
Principles of biomechanical posture analysis
Evaluation of static and dynamic human body conditions through engineering models and methodologies

assessment_methods.method: Evaluation of project activity (technical report, presentation, spreadsheet use)

assessment_rules: The overall assessment is a final grade based on the evaluation of the project activity for the software laboratory module and a written and/or oral examination for the applied mechanics module. For the project activity, correctness of methodology, application of Applied Mechanics knowledge, quality of numerical modeling, interpretation of results, and software proficiency are considered. For the examination, knowledge and understanding of human biomechanics principles, methodologies for analyzing stresses, application of theoretical concepts to problem-solving, correctness of knowledge, interpretation of results, and clarity of presentation are evaluated.
